To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of aspartic acids in SiFAlin-PEG-TATE derivatives does not influence SSTR binding, but does influence the radiotracer lipophilicity and renal clearance.

(1) the number of aspartic acids does not affect the in vitro SSTR binding potential, and (2) the addition of aspartic acid moieties to SiFAlin-peptides increases the hydrophilicity and leads to a slowed renal clearance and higher absolute tumor uptake in vivo, which results in a better tumor visualization by PET.

the number of aspartic acids does not affect the receptor binding potential of the SiFAlin-based TATE derivative, but that it can be used as a structure element to improve pharmacokinetic properties such as renal clearance and tumor uptake.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel SiFA-(18)F-labelable TATE derivative with a high potential for clinical translation, as it is able to provide a high tumor-to-background ratio and excellent tumor visualization by (18)F-PET.
the development of a new generation of SiFAlins that are able to increase the hydrophilicity and thus to slow down the renal clearance of SiFAlated peptides.

the development of novel SiFAlin-based (18)F-TATE derivatives and the determination of the influence of the molecular design of SiFAlins on the in vivo behavior of the resulting (SiFAlin-(18)F)-TATE derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a higher number of aspartic acids in the linker between SiFAlin and PEG does not affect the receptor binding affinity of SiFA-TATE derivatives but leads to a decreased renal clearance and a more favorable pharmacokinetic profile.

(i) the applied SiFA-labeling strategy is highly suited for the (18)F-radiolabeling of TATE analogs, (ii) aspartic acids can be used for the purpose of increasing hydrophilicity, and (iii) the applied molecular design of SiFAlins is well-suited for the development of (18) F-labeled SSTR-targeting TATE analogs
the number of aspartic acids does not influence the in vitro SSTR binding potential, whereas the number of PEG spacers does affect the in vivo pharmacokinetical properties of the radiotracer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SiFAlin-PEG1-Tyr(3)-octeotate [(18)F]-6 radiotracer is the most promising candidate for clinical translation of all SiFAlin-based TATE radiotracers.
the SiFAlin-based (18)F-radiolabeling approach is a promising strategy to obtain novel (18)F-TATE derivatives with favorable properties for the imaging of SSTR-positive tumors.
the introduction of a SiFAlin-based backbone and the use of a suitable linker between the peptide and SiFAlin moiety are essential for the development of SiFA-(18)F-labled TATE derivatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SiFAlin-PEG1-Tyr(3)-octeotactic acid derivative [(18) F]6 is a promising radiotracer for the visualization of SSTR-positive tumors by PET imaging.
a careful selection of molecular design elements is essential for the development of radiotracers with optimal properties for PET imaging.
a systematic approach in the design and optimization of peptidomimetic radiotracers is crucial for the development of highly potent radiopharmaceuticals.
